references.title: Gneiting, Making and Evaluating Point Forecasts
references.verified_support: Full primary PDF checked: consistent scoring targets require matching the statistical functional; this study uses mean with squared error and fixed quantiles for asymmetric piecewise-linear action costs. No statistical maturity follows from matching the target.

references.title: Bracher et al., Evaluating epidemic forecasts in an interval format
references.verified_support: Section2.2 distinguishes interval width, underprediction and overprediction penalties and builds WIS from median plus weighted interval scores; section2.3 supports averaging scores over targets. Here the exact three-interval weights and layer denominator are the L02 contract's.

references.title: Bracher et al., 2022 correction
references.verified_support: The formal correction was read along with the primary article. This candidate uses explicitly coded interval penalties and contract weights rather than inferring scoring direction from illustrative figures.

references.title: Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, FPP3: time series cross-validation
references.verified_support: Section5.10 uses successively earlier-only training sets and permits multi-step forecast errors. This study strengthens event-time ordering to the actual release-time/revision permission rule for each pseudo-origin.

references.title: Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, FPP3: hierarchical forecasting
references.verified_support: The hierarchy chapter defines coherent forecasts as adding up according to the aggregation structure. This study constructs aggregate samples and means bottom-up; marginal quantiles need not add.

references.title: NumPy quantile documentation
references.verified_support: The linear interpolation method uses fractional index(q*(n-1)); the code explicitly selects method=linear. The runtime NumPy version is independently recorded by the development execution.
